event.canonical_title: Zambia's Presidential Election: Hakainde Hichilema Expected to Secure Second Term
event.summary: Zambians are set to vote in a general election with President Hakainde Hichilema anticipated to win a second term. He faces 14 challengers, including main opposition candidate Brian Mundubile. Hichilema's campaign focuses on his economic record amid rising living costs and public dissatisfaction, while concerns about opposition intimidation have also emerged.

timeline.title: Zambia Halts Vote Counting Amid Violence and Ballot Theft Reports
timeline.summary: Zambia's electoral commission has suspended the counting of votes from the recent presidential and parliamentary elections due to violence directed at polling staff and reports of stolen marked ballots. The commission plans to reassess the situation within 24 hours. The main opposition candidate has expressed concern over the delays in the vote counting process.

timeline.title: Zambians Vote in Presidential Election Amid Economic Concerns
timeline.summary: Zambians voted on Thursday in a presidential election that tests the economic reforms of incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema. Approximately 8 million registered voters also selected members of Parliament and local councilors. Vote counting is currently underway, with results expected on Monday.

timeline.title: Vote Counting Resumes in Zambia After Violence Disruption
timeline.summary: Zambia has resumed vote counting following a nationwide suspension due to election-related violence, which included attacks on polling staff and the theft of marked ballot papers. The Electoral Commission reported that security threats have been contained. Official presidential results are anticipated soon, with opposition leader Brian Mundubile expressing concerns about transparency during the process.
key_facts: Vote counting was suspended due to violence during the election process.
The Electoral Commission stated that security threats have been contained.
Official presidential results are expected shortly.

event_overview.title: About Zambia Elections
event_overview.subject: Zambia Elections
event_overview.summary: Zambia’s 2026 general election is the nationwide vote to choose the President and other national and local officeholders. The presidential contest elects a President and Vice-President running mate; the outcome is determined under Zambia’s constitutional majoritarian system and administered by the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ).

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The first ballot was held nationwide in Zambia on Thursday, August 13, 2026, the constitutionally scheduled second Thursday of August for a general election held every five years.

facts.label: Offices covered
facts.value: A Zambian general election combines elections for President, Members of Parliament, mayors, council chairpersons and councillors on the same day.

facts.label: Presidential voting system
facts.value: The President is elected directly by registered voters with a Vice-President as running mate. A candidate must receive more than 50% of valid votes; otherwise, the top two candidates proceed to a second ballot within 37 days.

facts.label: Election authority
facts.value: The ECZ is the constitutional electoral management body responsible for implementing the electoral process, conducting elections, registering voters, accrediting observers and agents, and regulating electoral conduct.

facts.label: Results process
facts.value: The ECZ’s revised roadmap scheduled receipt and verification of results for August 15–17, 2026, followed by declaration of results on August 17; this timetable describes the planned process rather than a final outcome.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows immediate developments around polling, counting and disruptions in the August 2026 presidential vote; it does not provide a complete account of all races, campaigns, legal challenges or final certified results.
